key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni–20Cr+40TiC reduced oxidation weight gain by 95.71% versus bare SA516 boiler steel, delivering the best oxidation resistance among the tested coatings.
engineering_relevance: These coatings could improve SA516 boiler steel protection in high-temperature oxidizing environments by limiting oxide growth and spalling.
method: Applied Ni–20Cr, Ni–20Cr+40TiC, and Ni–20Cr+40TiN coatings using HVOF and plasma spray.
Characterized microstructure and phases using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: Laboratory testing linked improved oxidation resistance to protective Cr2O3, TiO2, NiTiO4, and NiO layers, reduced porosity, and enhanced microhardness.
watch_item: Performance over 50 laboratory cycles in air does not establish long-term durability under boiler-service corrosion and erosion conditions.
paper_title: Microstructure and High-Temperature Oxidation Behaviour of HVOF and Plasma Sprayed Ni–Cr-Based Ceramic Coatings on SA516 Boiler Steel
